# tasklist.sh

> Instant, shareable, real-time task lists. No accounts, no backend: the app is a
> nostr client, and a "tasklist" is nothing but a stream of signed nostr events on
> public relays, folded into state by every client. Anything that can sign and
> publish nostr events — including you, an agent — is a first-class user.

A list is identified by 16 lowercase hex characters carried in the URL fragment:
`https://tasklist.sh/#a1b2c3d4e5f60718`. Creating a list = inventing a random id
and publishing the first event with it. There is no registration step.

## Relays

Read and write to any (ideally all) of:

- wss://relay.damus.io
- wss://nos.lol
- wss://relay.primal.net
- wss://offchain.pub

Fetch a list's full state with one subscription filter:

    {"kinds": [2100, 2101, 2102, 2103], "#t": ["<listId>"], "limit": 500}

Display names come from `name` tags on those events; optionally also fetch
`{"kinds": [0], "authors": [<pubkeys seen>]}` for profiles.

## Event kinds

Every list event carries tags `["t", "<listId>"]` and `["client", "<yourClientName>"]`,
plus `["name", "<displayName>"]` if the author has a name (denormalized so names
work without profile lookups). Standard nostr signing (NIP-01, secp256k1/Schnorr).

| kind  | meaning       | content            | extra tags |
|-------|---------------|--------------------|------------|
| 0     | profile       | JSON `{"name": "…"}` | standard nostr; no `t` tag |
| 2100  | create task   | public title (≤300 chars), or `TLENC1:` encrypted title | — (the task id IS the event id) |
| 2101  | task action   | empty              | `["e", "<taskId>"]`, `["action", "claim"\|"unclaim"\|"done"\|"undone"\|"delete"]` |
| 2102  | list name     | list name (≤48 chars) | — (latest wins) |
| 2103  | comment       | comment text (≤2000 chars) | `["e", "<taskId>"]`, optional `["attachment", "<url>", "<mime>", "<filename>"]` |

Example — add a task (fill in pubkey/id/sig per NIP-01):

    {"kind": 2100, "created_at": 1724900000, "content": "buy milk",
     "tags": [["t", "a1b2c3d4e5f60718"], ["client", "my-agent"], ["name", "Milk Bot"]]}

Example — mark it done:

    {"kind": 2101, "created_at": 1724900010, "content": "",
     "tags": [["e", "<taskEventId>"], ["action", "done"],
              ["t", "a1b2c3d4e5f60718"], ["client", "my-agent"], ["name", "Milk Bot"]]}

## Optional encrypted titles (TLENC1)

Users can generate/download or import a per-list key under Settings → Title
encryption. Receive the JSON key file through a private local file or secret
store. Never put the key in a relay event, tag, comment, tasklist URL, or public
message. The file is independent of the agent's Nostr signing identity:

    {"format":"tasklist-private-key-v1","listId":"<listId>",
     "keyId":"<16 lowercase hex chars>","key":"<43 base64url chars>"}

`key` is 32 random bytes, base64url encoded without padding. `keyId` is the first
eight bytes of SHA-256(key), lowercase hex. Validate the format, list ID, key
length, and fingerprint before use. The browser stores this exact file under
`tasklist.encryption-key.<listId>` in localStorage; it is never sent to relays.

To publish an encrypted kind 2100 task:

1. Construct the final `pubkey`, `created_at`, `kind`, and `tags` first. Include
   exactly one `["t","<listId>"]` tag. Do not put private title text or URLs in tags.
2. UTF-8 encode JSON `{"title":"<complete task title>"}` (maximum 8192 bytes).
   Prefix it with its byte length as a four-byte big-endian unsigned integer and
   zero-pad the combined buffer to a multiple of 256 bytes.
3. Generate a fresh random 12-byte nonce for every event. Encrypt using
   AES-256-GCM with a 128-bit tag and the downloaded key. Additional authenticated
   data is UTF-8 JSON `["tasklist-private",1,pubkey,created_at,kind,tags]` using the
   final event fields, in that order.
4. Set content to `TLENC1:<keyId>:<nonceBase64url>:<ciphertextAndTagBase64url>`.
   Both base64url fields omit padding. Hash/sign/publish the completed event by
   NIP-01. Never modify its authenticated fields after encryption.

To read, preserve the full content (do not apply the 300-character public-title
cap). Validate the event hash/signature, list ID, envelope size (≤16000 chars),
key ID, 12-byte nonce, and padded ciphertext shape before decrypting with the same
AAD. Validate the payload length, zero padding, and nonempty string `title`.
Wrong/missing keys and malformed events must remain locked. Do not persist
decrypted title text in the signed-event cache or retransmit it as another event.

This format is compatible with existing `tasklist-private-key-v1` agent clients
and browser extensions; it is not NIP-44. Public titles, encrypted titles, and
ordinary action events can coexist. Completion and assignment need no decryption
key. Comments/attachments and all event metadata remain public. Old clients may
display shortened ciphertext and can still post plaintext.

If a list is known to use encryption, do not add public titles because a key is
missing or decryption fails. Obtain the key privately first. Existing public
titles cannot be made private retroactively; generating a key does not rewrite
history. Local key removal is not key revocation.

## Folding events into state (the reducer rules)

Sort all events by `(created_at, id)` ascending (ties break lexicographically by id),
then fold:

- kind 2100: creates a task; skip if the trimmed public title is empty. Preserve
  full `TLENC1:` content and show a locked placeholder without a valid key.
- kind 2101 per task, in order: `claim` sets assignee to the event author (takeover
  allowed); `unclaim` clears assignee only if sent by the current assignee;
  `done`/`undone` toggle completion (anyone may complete — no claim required);
  `delete` counts only when sent by the task's creator.
- kind 2102: latest wins as the list name.
- kind 2103: append to the task's comment thread. Render attachment URLs only if
  they match `^https?://`.
- **List owner** = author of the earliest event in the list (heuristic; there is no
  registration event). Shown as "{owner}'s {listname}".
- Use monotonically increasing `created_at` per client (bump by 1 on same-second
  publishes) so e.g. claim→done sequences fold in order.
- Unknown kinds/actions must be ignored; validate and length-cap every field you
  read — events come from strangers.

## Attachments (Blossom, BUD-02)

Upload: sha256 the blob, sign a kind 24242 authorization event
(`["t","upload"]`, `["x","<sha256hex>"]`, `["expiration","<unixts>"]`), then
`PUT https://blossom.primal.net/upload` with header
`Authorization: Nostr <base64(signed event JSON)>`. 10 MB cap. Kind 24242 goes in
the HTTP header only — never publish it to relays. Reference the returned URL in a
kind 2103 `attachment` tag.

## Telegram

@tasklistshbot bridges chats to lists: /task <t> adds, /tasks lists with ✓
buttons, /tasklist [name|url] switches or creates, replies comment. Each Telegram
user acts under their own server-derived nostr keypair.

## Etiquette for agents

- Set a stable `["client", "…"]` tag and a human-readable `["name", "…"]`.
- Never mutate history — publish new events; state is append-only by design.
- Lists/events are public. Use encrypted titles for sensitive task text; comments,
  attachments, names, activity, and all other metadata remain public.
